newsitem.title: USA: Capstar to buy firm, 36 radio stations for $215mln.
newsitem.headline: Capstar to buy firm, 36 radio stations for $215mln.

text.p: Capstar Broadcasting Partners, an investment group formed by Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst Inc, has signed a letter of intent to buy Patterson Broadcasting Inc and its 36 middle-market radio stations in a deal valued at about $215 million, the companies announced Wednesday.
The majority stake in Atlanta-based Patterson is owned by Dyson Kissner Moran Corp, a New York-based private investment firm.
The deal is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 1998, the companies said.
Thomas Hicks, chairman and chief executive officer of Hicks Muse, said that with the firm's latest deal, Capstar is now the largest radio group in the country, based on station count.
The transaction is subject to the execution of definitive agreement, approval by the Federal Communications Commission and other customary closing conditions, they added.

Capstar said the acquisition will raise the number of radio stations it now owns or has agreements to buy to 156 and brings the value of all acquisitions completed or announced since its formation in May 1996 to about $785 million.

Capstar said Patterson owns or has agreements to acquire 36 radio stations in Honolulu; Savannah, Ga.; Battle Creek, Mich.; Pensacola, Fla; Grand Rapids, Mich.; Springfield, Ill.; Fresno, Calif.; Reno, Nev.; Allentown, Penn.; and Harrisburg, Pa. It also is in talks to acquire five additional stations.

Patterson's president and chief executive officer, James Wesley Jr and the company's chief financial officer, James Strawn, have agreed to join Capstar's senior management after the transaction, Capstar said.
R. Steven Hicks will continue to be president and CEO of Capstar, it said.
